pricing.freeTierCaps: 20 saved words/phrases, 5 imported lessons, and 1 audio playlist; library access in 50+ languages
pricing.billingTerms: Premium monthly, 12-month, or 24-month prepaid terms; Premium Plus monthly or annual; auto-renews by storefront

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For LingQ Premium, import permitted text and audio, mark known words, and review vocabulary in context. The hard boundary is content library, import pipeline, multi-device sync, community, tutors, and polish, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Import permitted text and audio, mark known words, review vocabulary in context, schedule retrieval practice from a study plan, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: content library, import pipeline, multi-device sync, community, tutors, and polish
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for LingQ Premium because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for LingQ Premium in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import permitted text and audio, mark known words, review vocabulary in context, schedule retrieval practice from a study plan, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
